narrative:
Round 21 (Days 19-22) consolidated post-Weimar Triangle momentum while exposing persistent fault lines. The DK-DE-PL Baltic Sea Security Dialogue (Copenhagen, Day 21) established coordinated maritime domain awareness framework without triggering Russian escalation. US THAAD deployment Romania (Day 22) validated dual-flank deterrence architecture. Turkey's F-35 timeline demand (March 15 vs March 31) created friction requiring swift US resolution. Russia accepted NFIU-RO rotational framework while expanding Zapad-2026 to 95K troops. China increased Taiwan sorties to 100/day. Hungary withdrew from London Ministerial, signaling continued obstruction.

DK-DE-PL Copenhagen dialogue produced joint communiqué establishing Baltic Sea Coordination Framework: Danish Straits control + German mechanized presence + Polish corridor coordination + Norwegian P-8 ASW = comprehensive domain awareness without permanent naval facilities. Germany committed €300M rail standardization (Rotterdam-Warsaw-Suwalki corridor), Denmark maintained Straits closure to Russian military vessels, Poland allocated storage/security for US GMLRS Rzeszow (500 rounds arrived Day 21-22). Norwegian P-8 integration (2 sorties/week Kaliningrad monitoring) created standing Baltic Sea surveillance architecture. The framework avoided Russian red line (no permanent naval bases) while institutionalizing coordination.

US THAAD battery arrived Romania MK Air Base Day 22 (120 personnel, AN/TPY-2 radar, 48 interceptors), integrating with Deveselu Aegis Ashore. Romania-Turkey Black Sea maritime coordination launched Day 21 with joint intelligence cell at Constanta. Romania deployed expanded NFIU-RO liaison team (12 officers: 3 intel, 2 air defense, 2 logistics, 1 cyber) to Bucharest. Poland's Deputy Defense Minister arrived Bucharest Day 19 for NFIU-RO force generation planning. Czech 25K rounds (Belgian-funded) logistics prep Days 21-24 for Day 25 Lithuania delivery. Netherlands 43rd Brigade June deployment logistics planning accelerated.

Turkey demanded F-35 timeline clarification: March 15, 2027 first aircraft delivery vs March 31, 2027 contract signature. Ankara deployed 150-troop reconnaissance element to Lithuania Day 21 as good-faith gesture but threatened Swedish ratification delays absent timeline clarity. US faced choice: accelerate to March 15 delivery (reward Turkey's 3,500-troop commitment) or maintain March 31 schedule (Congressional skepticism about Ankara reliability). Decision: March 15 contract signature with first 4 F-35As October 2026 delivery, remaining 36 on 2027-2029 schedule. Turkey accepted, Swedish ratification scheduled March 2026 parliament.

Russia's strategic response demonstrated calibrated acceptance. Foreign Ministry statement Day 20: 'Russia views rotational troop presence as distinct from permanent infrastructure. NFIU-RO rotational framework consistent with 1997 Founding Act. Permanent NATO naval facilities in Baltic approaches would violate regional security architecture.' Zapad-2026 expanded from 75K to 95K troops (Western Military District, Belarus, Kaliningrad, September) — signal of resolve without immediate escalation. GRU intensified monitoring of DK-DE-PL dialogue for permanent maritime facilities (none detected). Kaliningrad refit Day 21/60 on schedule.

China increased Taiwan Strait sorties from 85/day to 100/day (Days 19-22), deploying 6-ship Type 052D destroyer blocking formation east of Taiwan. PLA Eastern Theater Command shifted from exercise tempo to permanent posture — sustained pressure without invasion trigger. FM Wang Yi Budapest visit scheduled Days 23-24 (moved up from Days 10-12) to prep Xi-Orban summit Day 25. Beijing's economic leverage: signal €75B EU debt purchase expansion contingent on NFIU-RO restraint.

Hungary withdrew from London Defense Ministerial Day 7 (announced Day 20), refusing to endorse EFP 2.0 formalization. Budapest signaled 'constructive abstention' on April Ukraine aid package (vs outright veto) in exchange for EU recovery fund unfreeze. Orban's calculation: 1% war support prohibits NATO operations, so obstruction costs nothing domestically while deepening China-Russia partnerships yields economic benefits.

Nordic force integration advanced. Swedish CV90 live-fire exercise Day 21 with Finnish participation demonstrated mechanized interoperability. Denmark hosted Copenhagen dialogue, establishing Nordic-Baltic maritime coordination. All four Nordics (FI, SE, NO, DK) committed 150 troops each to NFIU force identification (total 600), conditional on €2B NATO Baltic infrastructure fund. Finnish war support 65% (highest Nordic) enabled leadership; Norwegian 47% (lowest) constrained to intelligence/logistics roles.

Baltics prepared for US Patriot arrivals Day 25. Lithuania conducted site prep Rukla/Kaunas Air Bases Days 21-24. Latvia reinforced Canadian EFP with National Guard battalions. Estonia CCDCOE provided NATO intelligence assessment: Kaliningrad refit creates 30% naval capability gap through Day 60, opportunity for increased NATO Baltic Sea presence. Estonia deployed 25-personnel signals intelligence team monitoring Russian Kaliningrad communications.

Czech Republic 7th Mechanised Brigade deployment timeline finalized: 850 troops arriving Lithuania Days 30-35 (Pandur II APCs, T-72M4CZ tanks). President Pavel advocated at London Ministerial (attended Day 7 despite Hungary withdrawal) for 14-day maximum deployment windows. Czech-Polish-Lithuanian ammunition coordination group established targeting 50K rounds/month by Q3 2026. Belgian 25K rounds transfer funded Czech production, delivery Day 25.

Canada extended Operation REASSURANCE funding CAD$200M, committed 350 additional troops Lithuania (Day 35 deployment). Canadian Intelligence Fusion Cell deployed Rukla for C2 restoration. Netherlands allocated €45M Lithuanian infrastructure (rail/road corridors), Rotterdam NATO logistics cell operational. Romania committed 450-troop mechanized battalion (Day 50-55 deployment), linked Baltic-Black Sea security at London Ministerial.

UK deployed additional 600 troops Lithuania (total 1,800+), £150M Baltic infrastructure fund, 6 Typhoons Estonia Amari (90-day rotation Day 25). France committed 150 troops from 11th Para (Day 35), €200M reconstruction, hosted Weimar Triangle Paris Days 24-25. Germany participated Copenhagen dialogue, committed additional 400-troop Panzer battalion Lithuania (Day 20 deployment — 1 day early), €300M infrastructure (€800M total).

Oil declined to $87/barrel (down from $88 Round 20, continued market confidence). Corridor 85% capacity maintained. GMLRS Rzeszow: 500 rounds arrived Days 21-22, Poland provided secure storage. Patriot batteries Poland/Lithuania: advance logistics Days 21-24, deployment Day 25. Belgium hosted NAC Perm Reps session Day 25 (moved up from March 1) on EFP 2.0 burden-sharing.

Key metric shifts: Oil $87 (down from $88), corridor 85% (stable), China Taiwan sorties 100/day (up from 85), Russia Zapad-2026 95K troops (up from 75K), Turkey F-35 timeline resolved (March 15 contract, October 2026 first delivery), Hungary London Ministerial withdrawal.
